question.problem: Find all of the real solutions to the equation $8{z}^{3}-{z}^{2}+40z-5=0.$
question.worked_solution:
We proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}8{z}^{3}-{z}^{2}+40z-5 & = \\ (8{z}^{3}-{z}^{2})+(40z-5) & = \\ {z}^{2}(8z-1)+5(8z-1) & = \\ (8z-1)\cdot {z}^{2}+(8z-1)\cdot 5 & = \\ (8z-1)({z}^{2}+5) & .\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve $(8z-1)({z}^{2}+5)=0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

- Setting the factor $(8z-1)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8z-1 & =0 \\ 8z & =1 \\ z & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $({z}^{2}+5)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}+5 & =0 \\ {z}^{2} & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since a squared real number cannot be negative, the equation ${z}^{2}+5=0$ has no real solutions.

Therefore,  $z=\frac{1}{8}$ is the only real solution.
